verifier_note: Every one of the 13 citations resolved to a real source and zero were fabricated: 3 arXiv abs+PDF (incl. 2606.17126, which does exist and is TASLP-accepted), 6 DOIs via Crossref/OpenAlex/PMC/publisher PDF, the ICPhS 1999 proceedings PDF, and the live vendor/repo docs. The paywalled vocology numbers are unusually clean - Prame, Ferrante, Collyer, Nestorova, Faghih and Stasak match their sources digit-for-digit once I reconstructed the OpenAlex inverted-index abstracts myself (a WebFetch summariser first returned a mangled Prame abstract of '+/-134 ... +/-171 cent', and separately invented an entire results table for VibE-SVC2, so no number here rests on a summariser). The systemic problem is version drift and one false negative: the Synthesizer V surface is quoted perfectly but from the discontinued Studio 1 manual, and the lane's headline claim that no system takes an absolute vibrato spec is falsified by OpenUtau's own per-note vibrato (period in ms, depth in cents), which feeds the f0 that the DiffSinger renderer consumes.

verdicts.verify_note: Every value matches the sv1 manual exactly (Freq 1-10 Hz d.5.5; Depth 0-2 st d.1; Start 0-1 s d.0.25; 0.1/0.07 s portamento; PitchDev +/-1200 c; Loudness -inf..+24 dB). But sv1 is Studio 1; Studio 2 Pro discontinued Manual Mode.

corrections.claim: Scope the whole parametric surface to Synthesizer V Studio 1, not to 'the shipping commercial neural SVS'. Studio 2 Pro shipped 21 March 2025 and Studio 1 Pro was withdrawn from sale; the Studio 2 manual states 'Manual Mode has been discontinued in Version 2' and that 'while vibrato was specified by numerical values in Manual Mode, version 2 allows for intuitive editing of vibrato depth and frequency using the Smart Pitch Controls'. In Studio 2 the numeric Vibrato (Start/Left/Right/Depth/Freq/Phase/Jitter) and Pitch Transition (Offset/Duration L-R/Depth L-R) blocks no longer exist; what survives is Vibrato Modulation 0.00-2.00 default 1.00, the Expression Pad, AI Retakes, drag-based Smart Pitch Controls, and Pitch Deviation, which the manual describes as 'primarily used to maintain compatibility with previous versions'. Base Parameters in Studio 2 publish no min/max/default figures at all and add Mouth Opening. Separately, the design implication's 'mutually exclusive modes' is not what the sv1 manual says: switching Manual mode on moves the AI-generated curve into Pitch Deviation, where it is summed with the manual curve rather than discarded.

verdicts.verify_note: v2.3.0 = 2024-03-11; voicing/tension defs, config flags and curve list (GENC 12 st/100, VELC x2/100, PEXP 0-100 d.100) all exact. False half: OpenUtau's per-note UVibrato takes period 5-500 ms and depth 5-200 cents.

corrections.claim: The absence claim holds only for the drawable expression curves, not for OpenUtau. OpenUtau master defines a per-note UVibrato whose source comments read 'Period in milliseconds' (clamped 5-500 ms, i.e. 2-200 Hz) and 'Depth in cents (1 semitone = 100 cents)' (clamped 5-200 cents), plus length %, fade in/out %, shift, drift and volume linkage; the shipped default preset 'Standard' is length 75%, period 175 ms (about 5.7 Hz), depth 25 cents. RenderPhrase.cs evaluates that vibrato into the pitches[] array in cents ('Use tempo at note start to calculate vibrato period'), and DiffSingerRenderer.cs samples phrase.pitches directly as the 'f0' ONNX input. So the open route does accept an absolute numeric vibrato specification in Hz-equivalent and cents, and the design implication that honouring a notated vibrato requires synthesising the F0 contour yourself and feeding it as PITD is wrong.

verdicts.verify_note: arXiv:2509.07038, 8 Sep 2025, Ryu/Shin/Kim. Abstract carries verbatim 'the first attempt enabling user-driven dynamics control in SVS' and 'over 50% reduction in mean absolute error of energy sequences for phoneme-level inputs'.

All figures exact in the v6 PDF: 6 techniques, 294 h (36/30/85/85/18), 40 unseen singers, 76.1/76.1/79.9%, MOS-Q 4.05+/-0.10, MOS-C 4.18+/-0.08; GTSinger 80.59 h, 20 pros, 9 languages. Venue is EMNLP 2024, not 2025.

corrections.claim: Only the year is wrong. arXiv v1 is 24 September 2024; the arXiv comment field reads 'Accepted by EMNLP 2024' and the journal_ref is 'Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pages 1960-1975'. The 2025 date is the v6 revision, not the publication. Substance stands: no numeric vibrato rate or extent input exists anywhere in the model, and the per-technique recognition accuracies behind the 76.1% control figure are vibrato 0.89 / glissando 0.85 / falsetto 0.84 / pharyngeal 0.80 / mixed voice 0.78 / breathy 0.78.

verdicts.verify_note: PDF: 'VibE-SVC was limited to vibrato extent scaling'; alpha optimum ~3.0, beta sharp drop past 2.0 = 'mechanical vibration'; 'typical singing vibrato has a range of 3-9 Hz'; Acc .736/.725/.747, ZS .614. N = 20 VocalSet singers (11M/9F).

JASA 102:616-21 abstract: 25 tones from ten commercial CDs of Schubert's Ave Maria; per-tone extent +/-34 to +/-123 c, mean across tones and singers +/-71 c; neg. corr. duration, pos. intonation. N = 25 tones, 10 pro lyric singers.

JASA 130:1683-8 abstract: -1.8+/-0.3 Hz/century, +56.4+/-0.3 cent/century, r = -0.62, rate rise near tone end, weak positive duration-extent link. N = 100+ recordings of one tone by 75 soprano recording artists.

J Voice abstract: 15 professional operatic/musical-theater/jazz mezzos and sopranos, 2 cross-genre songs + 1 exercise, 16 pitch segments each, Praat; CV of mean half-extent separated genre, higher in MT/jazz; 7 pedagogue judges agreed.

ICPhS99 p.981 confirms 81% rising VO, pro 4.41-4.86 Hz vs jg 7.12 / mr 7.20 Hz, and settling more variable in less-trained voices. But the A3 excursion contrast is wrong. N = 5 male singers, one recorded twice.

corrections.claim: The 'professional 33.57 Hz versus 12.47-19.55 Hz for the trained-student and choral voices' contrast does not survive Table 5/7. A3 VO(exc) by voice is db 33.57, db2 12.47, tv 39.52, jg -10.39, mb 14.86, mr 19.55, group mean 21.73 Hz. db2 is the same professional baritone after warmup, not a student or choral voice, so 12.47 belongs to the professional; and the trained student tv measured 39.52 Hz, the largest excursion in the study, above the professional's 33.57. The paper's own profile for tv reads 'Range and excursion above average'. Also, only A3 was a held tone: D3 data came from the lowest tone of falling D4-D3 arpeggios, sung on [i] [e] [a] [o] at mf. Everything else stands: 81% of productions show rising VO, first-five-cycle rate 4.41/4.60/4.86 Hz for the professional against jg 7.12 and mr 7.20 Hz on A3 (the paper calls these 'the untrained voice jg and the actor mr'), and settling time 'more variable among less trained than among more trained singers'.

verdicts.verify_note: JASA 121:1728-36 abstract: 'Five trained female classical singers performed a total of 318 messe di voce'; SPL change predominantly nonlinear, cres/decres traces differ; spectral balance (0-2 vs 2-4 kHz) more symmetric than linear.
